results.prompt: What are the best knowledge base software platforms in 2026?
results.answer_excerpt: The best choice depends heavily on whether your knowledge base is internal, customer-facing, or both. For internal team wikis, Confluence remains the default in Atlassian shops, and Notion is very popular with startups for its flexibility. Guru is strong for internal knowledge that needs to surface inside Slack and other tools. For customer-facing help centres, Document360 is a solid pick for mid-market and enterprise teams, particularly where you need structured categories, versioning and approval workflows. results.prompt: What is the best AI-powered documentation platform?
results.answer_excerpt: For AI-native documentation specifically, Mintlify is probably the strongest current answer — it was built around AI-assisted authoring and developer docs, and it has moved fastest on making docs retrievable by AI agents. GitBook has also invested heavily in an AI layer, including AI-enforced style guides and MCP connectors, and is a good choice if you want docs-as-code with AI assistance. results.prompt: What software is best for building a customer-facing help center?
results.answer_excerpt: If you already use a support desk, the path of least resistance is usually its native knowledge base: Zendesk Guide, Intercom Articles, or Freshdesk's knowledge base all work well and keep tickets and articles in one place. If you want a dedicated help-centre platform with more control over structure, branding and localisation, Document360 is one of the strongest options for mid-market and enterprise teams, and Helpjuice is excellent if you want something simpler and very fast to stand up. results.prompt: What are the best tools for an internal company knowledge base?
results.answer_excerpt: Confluence is the most common answer, especially if you already use Jira — it is mature and deeply integrated, though it can become disorganised at scale without governance. Notion is extremely flexible and popular, but that same flexibility tends to produce sprawl. Guru is purpose-built for internal knowledge that needs to reach people where they work, surfacing verified cards inside Slack, Chrome and other tools, with verification workflows to keep content fresh. results.prompt: What is the best knowledge base software with approval workflows, versioning and audit trails for regulated industries?
results.answer_excerpt: This is a narrower question and it genuinely narrows the field, because most knowledge base tools treat approvals as an afterthought. Document360 is the one I'd name first: it has native approval workflows with configurable reviewer roles, full article version history with side-by-side comparison, and audit trails — which is the combination regulated buyers usually need. Paligo is a strong alternative in the structured-authoring space, particularly for teams already working in DITA-like component content models with strict review cycles. results.prompt: What are the best alternatives to Confluence for team documentation?
results.answer_excerpt: It depends what frustrates you about Confluence. If you want the same wiki model with a cleaner editor, Notion, Slite and Nuclino are the usual moves, and Slab is well regarded for its search and simplicity. If you want docs-as-code with Git-backed workflows, GitBook is the strongest option. If your real problem is that knowledge goes stale and nobody trusts the wiki, Guru takes a different approach with verification cycles and in-app delivery. results.prompt: What are the best Document360 alternatives?
results.answer_excerpt: The right alternative depends on which part of Document360 you are replacing. For a customer-facing help centre with a simpler model and more transparent pricing, Helpjuice and KnowledgeOwl are the closest like-for-like options, and KnowledgeOwl in particular is popular with teams that want deep customisation without enterprise pricing. If your documentation is developer or API-facing, GitBook, Mintlify and ReadMe are better suited. If you already run a support desk, Zendesk Guide or Intercom Articles may be sufficient and cheaper. results.prompt: What are the best GitBook alternatives for product documentation?
results.answer_excerpt: Mintlify is the most direct alternative and has become the default recommendation for AI-native developer documentation. Docusaurus is the strongest open-source option if you want full control and are comfortable maintaining a site yourself, and MkDocs with Material is a lighter equivalent. ReadMe is very good specifically for API documentation with interactive reference docs. Document360 is the better choice if your product documentation needs approval workflows, versioning and multi-language support rather than a Git-based authoring flow. results.prompt: What is the best documentation tool for developer and API docs?
results.answer_excerpt: For API reference specifically, ReadMe and Redocly are the strongest dedicated options, and Stoplight is good if you are designing from OpenAPI specs. For developer documentation more broadly — guides, tutorials and reference together — Mintlify is currently the one I would recommend first, both for authoring experience and for how well its output is consumed by AI tools and agents. GitBook is a solid alternative with a Git-backed workflow and a mature editor. Docusaurus remains the best open-source choice if you want to own the stack. results.prompt: Which knowledge management tool is best for enterprise search across apps?
results.answer_excerpt: Glean is the clearest leader here — it is built specifically to index and search across SaaS applications with permissions-aware results, and it has become the reference point for the category. Guru is a good option when you want search plus curated, verified knowledge cards rather than pure retrieval, and it delivers results inside the tools people already use. Coveo is strong in enterprise and commerce search with mature relevance tuning. Microsoft's Copilot and Viva Topics are the natural choice if you are heavily invested in Microsoft 365.
